selection_rule: FREEZE ADDENDUM 3 decomposition pass: 2 components per MIXED parent (candidate-real + surface) authored by a sealed frontier decomposer, plus FREEZE ADDENDUM 4 position-fingerprint channels; every component is routed INDEPENDENTLY by the blind audit

selected.name: Evidence of Correct, Complete Contribution
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the diff and plain-language explanation show that evidenced requirements are implemented, appropriate validation is present, behavior is coherent, and avoidable technical debt is not introduced. Give 0 when correctness, completeness, validation, or debt concerns remain, even if the description is long and impeccably templated. Judge substance only; do not reward headings, checklists, issue links, title conventions, description length, or template completion.
selected.rationale: This isolates functional completeness and maintainability from submission presentation. A terse three-sentence description with no template can be a 10 here and low on the surface component; an extensively templated, fully checklisted submission can be high on the surface component and 0 here.

selected.name: Submission-Norm Marker Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull request visibly contains many submission-hygiene markers, such as template sections, checklist items, structured headings, issue references, conventional title wording, and explicit status or test sections. Give 0 when these markers are absent. Count or estimate their presence and prominence only; do not decide whether they are useful, correct, or desirable.
selected.rationale: This measures the visible carrier rather than contribution substance. A bare but technically complete submission can be low here and high on the real component; a polished template with little substantive evidence can be high here and low on the real component.
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Contribution readiness and submission norms

selected.name: Requirement-Bounded Design Simplicity
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the implementation uses only mechanisms needed for the evidenced requirements, keeps boundaries and control flow understandable, and avoids speculative abstractions, unnecessary options, premature optimization, and incidental complexity. Give 0 when the design is materially over-engineered, speculative, or harder to reason about than necessary, regardless of explanatory prose. Judge the code and substantive design only; do not reward comment length, description length, or review-comment volume.
selected.rationale: This isolates actual design complexity from discussion volume and presentation. A simple implementation with sparse explanation can be high here and low on the surface component; a complex implementation accompanied by extensive tradeoff discussion can be high on the surface component and low here.

selected.name: Complexity-Discussion Surface Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull request contains extensive visible discussion of design, alternatives, tradeoffs, architecture, performance, or complexity across its title, description, and comments. Give 0 when such discussion is absent or minimal. Count or estimate the amount and prominence of this discussion only; do not judge whether it is insightful, accurate, or beneficial.
selected.rationale: This captures explanatory and interactional surface area without evaluating the implementation. A terse, genuinely simple change can be low here and high on the real component; a verbose discussion around an unnecessarily complex change can be high here and low on the real component.
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Simplicity (KISS/YAGNI) and complexity management

selected.name: Substantive Behavior-Preserving Refactoring
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the change materially improves structure or removes an identifiable design smell, preserves intended behavior, uses appropriate refactoring boundaries, and provides code or validation evidence that risk is controlled. Give 0 when the change is cosmetic-only, introduces behavioral uncertainty, lacks a meaningful structural rationale, or leaves avoidable risk. Judge refactoring substance only; do not reward addition/deletion ratio, title wording, headings, or comment length.
selected.rationale: This separates structural and behavioral value from the way refactoring is packaged. A meaningful refactor can be described tersely and score high here while low on the surface component; cosmetic churn with prominent refactor labeling can score high on the surface component and low here.

selected.name: Refactor-Presentation Marker Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull request visibly uses many refactor labels, summary annotations, before-and-after descriptions, structured refactor sections, explanatory comments, or separated structural change regions in the diff. Give 0 when these presentation markers are absent or minimal. Count or estimate visible packaging only; do not judge its clarity, value, or the refactor itself.
selected.rationale: This measures how strongly the submission signals and packages a refactor. A behavior-preserving refactor with a terse title and little annotation can be high on the real component and low here; cosmetic changes with abundant refactor markers can be high here and low on the real component.
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Refactoring quality and practice

selected.name: Semantically Useful Documentation
selected.instruction: Give 10 when documentation accurately explains behavior, constraints, rationale, or usage, is sufficient for a reader to act correctly, and has examples or comments that match the implementation. Give 0 when documentation is absent, misleading, purely decorative, or merely restates code without useful meaning. Judge communicative substance only; do not reward headers, lists, fences, fragments, doc-comment syntax, or document length.
selected.rationale: This isolates whether documentation helps readers understand and use the contribution. Useful documentation can be plain prose without formatting and score high here while low on the surface component; richly formatted documentation that says little can score high on the surface component and low here.

selected.name: Documentation-Format Marker Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the text visibly contains many formatting conventions, including headers, bulleted or numbered lists, structured steps, fenced multi-line code, concise summary fragments, and language-specific documentation-comment forms. Give 0 when these markers are absent or minimal. Count or estimate convention presence only; do not decide whether the formatting is appropriate, consistent, readable, or valuable.
selected.rationale: This captures document shape independently of semantic usefulness. Plain, accurate documentation can be high on the real component and low here; extensive headers, lists, and fenced blocks around inaccurate or empty content can be high here and low on the real component.
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Documentation formatting and style conventions

selected.name: Actionable Change Rationale
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the title and accompanying text accurately explain what changed, why it was needed, relevant constraints, expected effects, and review-relevant risks at a detail level proportionate to the change, without merely narrating the diff. Give 0 when context and rationale are missing, generic, misleading, or replaced by diff narration, even when the submission is lengthy and highly structured. Judge informational substance only; do not reward bullets, headings, issue references, templates, or word count.
selected.rationale: This isolates actionable context from communication scaffolding. A concise three-sentence explanation can be high here and low on the surface component; a long, bulleted, issue-linked description that says little can be high on the surface component and low here.

selected.name: Communication-Scaffolding Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull request visibly contains extensive communication scaffolding, such as long descriptions, multiple sections, many bullets, issue references, conventional title or message patterns, and other structured metadata. Give 0 when it is brief and largely unstructured with few or no such markers. Count or estimate visible form only; do not judge whether the communication is clear, sufficient, accurate, or useful.
selected.rationale: This measures communication shape rather than rationale quality. A brief but highly informative explanation can be high on the real component and low here; a long, heavily structured description with little substance can be high here and low on the real component.
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Change/commit/PR communication quality

selected.name: Conventionlessness Cue Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull-request text contains many explicit cues that the surrounding codebase lacks settled idioms, such as establishing a first pattern, choosing among competing conventions, or describing ad hoc structure. Give 0 when no such cues appear. Measure cue extent only; do not judge the contribution or whether conventionlessness is good or bad.
selected.rationale: This fingerprints an early or still-forming repository context through textual cues. It is not the construct because the same contribution can be technically strong or weak in either a conventionless or settled environment.
selected.upstream_parent: Early versus late arrival and codebase maturity

selected.name: Shared-History Presupposition Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the text heavily presupposes shared project history through references to longstanding components, prior migrations, recurring maintainer practices, internal shorthand, or ongoing conventions. Give 0 when the pull request is self-contained and contains no such presuppositions. Measure reliance on shared history only; do not judge whether that reliance improves communication or contribution quality.
selected.rationale: This fingerprints temporal embeddedness and accumulated project history. It is separate from contribution quality because a change may be excellent or poor regardless of how much prior history it assumes.
selected.upstream_parent: Late arrival and accumulated repository history

selected.name: Concurrent-Activity Cue Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull-request text contains many cues of surrounding activity, such as parallel changes, conflicts, release trains, backports, active migrations, deadlines, or coordination with other work. Give 0 when none of these cues appear. Measure textual evidence of concurrent repository activity only; do not judge urgency, organization, or contribution quality.
selected.rationale: This fingerprints how busy the repository was around the contribution. Activity pressure is contextual and does not itself indicate whether the proposed change is substantively good.
selected.upstream_parent: Repository busyness around the pull request

selected.name: Version-Era Anchor Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the pull request contains many concrete temporal anchors, including language, runtime, dependency, tooling, platform, deprecation, or migration versions that locate the work in the repository’s lifecycle. Give 0 when no such anchors are visible. Measure anchoring detail only; do not judge whether the versions or migration choices are appropriate.
selected.rationale: Version and migration vocabulary can locate a contribution within the repository’s historical development. The presence of such anchors is not a judgment about correctness, usefulness, or maintainability.
selected.upstream_parent: Temporal position and project lifecycle stage

selected.name: Automation-Generated Submission Extent
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the text strongly exhibits machine-generated submission signals, such as bot authorship, standardized dependency-update wording, generated changelog language, repetitive metadata, or formulaic update descriptions. Give 0 when no such signals are visible and the text appears individually authored. Measure automation-signature extent only; do not judge the contribution or the automation.
selected.rationale: Automated-submission signatures can fingerprint repository workflow and its historical automation practices. They are not part of contribution quality because automation can accompany either a substantive or insubstantial change.
selected.upstream_parent: Repository automation maturity and workflow era
